title.en: Choose a Key-Value Store or Cache: DynamoDB, ElastiCache/Valkey, and Edge Configuration

sources.title: Working with expired items and time to live (TTL)
supports: Expired items that are not filtered keep showing in read and write operations until the background process deletes them
Expired items still count towards storage and read costs until they are deleted
A filter expression on the TTL attribute removes expired items from Scan and Query results
sources.note: The parent page (source dynamodb-ttl) was re-read the same day: deletion is 'within a few days', 'typically within a few days after their expiration'.

sources.title: Working with items and attributes in DynamoDB
supports: UpdateItem can implement an atomic counter: a numeric attribute incremented without interfering with other write requests; all write requests are applied in the order received
Atomic counter updates are not idempotent, so a retried UpdateItem can overcount; the page recommends a conditional update where miscounting cannot be tolerated
A conditional write whose condition evaluates to false still consumes write capacity (a minimum of 1 unit)

sources.title: Using update expressions in DynamoDB
supports: ADD mathematically adds a number to an existing Number attribute, and sets the attribute to that number when it does not exist
ADD supports only number and set data types
An update expression can combine SET and ADD clauses

sources.title: Deploying DynamoDB locally on your computer
supports: DynamoDB Local is available as a downloadable archive with a published SHA-256 checksum, and as a Docker image
The downloadable version needs a Java Runtime Environment 17.x or newer
sources.note: The archive linked from this page was downloaded, its checksum compared, and run as version 3.3.1 for the store contract tests.

sources.title: What is Amazon ElastiCache?
supports: ElastiCache runs in two formats: serverless caches and node-based clusters, with the Valkey, Memcached, and Redis OSS engines
ElastiCache Serverless supports two connection types, VPC and Public; a public endpoint is reached over the internet without a VPC and requires IAM authentication and TLS 1.3 for every connection
The connection type is chosen when the cache is created
ElastiCache Serverless is compatible with Valkey 7.2 and later, Memcached 1.6.22 and later, and Redis OSS 7.1; public endpoints need Valkey 9.0 or later

sources.title: Choosing between deployment options
supports: Serverless operates engines in cluster mode enabled only; clients must support cluster mode
Serverless: clients connect to a single endpoint; encryption in transit and at rest are always enabled
Serverless: data is replicated asynchronously across multiple Availability Zones; durability (the Multi-AZ transactional log) is not supported
Node-based clusters: public endpoints are not supported; pricing is per node-hour, while serverless is billed for data stored in GB-hours and requests in ECPUs
Serverless configuration is limited to basic settings such as subnets, backups, and maximum cache usage limits

sources.title: Create a Valkey serverless cache with a public endpoint
supports: Public endpoints are available on ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey 9.0 or later
ElastiCache provides a system-managed IAM user (default.iam-user) and user group (default.iam-user-group); a custom group must contain only users that authenticate with IAM
The CLI example creates the cache with --engine valkey --major-engine-version 9 --connection-type public --user-group-id default.iam-user-group
The ability to create public caches can be restricted with the elasticache:ConnectionType condition key

sources.title: Connect to a cache with a public endpoint
supports: All public endpoint connections require IAM authentication and TLS 1.3
The caller needs elasticache:Connect on both the serverless cache ARN and the ElastiCache user ARN
Three ways to produce the token: the GLIDE client, the Developer Toolkit for ElastiCache (Python), or manual SigV4 signing

Tokens are valid for 15 minutes; with the toolkit or manual signing a new token is generated for each new connection; expiry does not affect established connections; a token signed with temporary credentials expires with them if sooner
Connections expire after 12 hours; revoking elasticache:Connect does not disconnect active sessions
Troubleshooting: WRONGPASS (expired token, wrong user, missing permission, cache name not lowercase), NOAUTH when a client sends a command before authenticating, TLS handshake failure without TLS 1.3

sources.title: Authenticating with IAM
supports: IAM authentication passes a short-lived token instead of a password in AUTH or HELLO; it needs Valkey 7.2 or above (or Redis OSS 7.0 or above) and in-transit encryption

The token is a SigV4 pre-signed GET request to http://<cache name>/ with query parameters Action=connect, User=<user id>, and ResourceType=ServerlessCache for serverless caches, signed for service elasticache with a 900-second expiry, with the http:// prefix removed
For IAM-enabled users the user name and user ID must be identical
Cache names are lowercased at creation, and the signing code must use the lowercase name
An IAM-authenticated connection is disconnected after 12 hours unless re-authenticated
GLIDE 2.2 and later generate, cache, and refresh the token themselves
sources.note: The reference implementation on the page is Java. The sample's TypeScript signer follows it and was never presented to ElastiCache.

sources.title: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
supports: ElastiCache users carry an access string and belong to user groups, which are attached to caches
ElastiCache configures a default user with full access; the page tells you to replace it with one that is disabled or has a strong password
The nopass option is not recommended

sources.title: ElastiCache in-transit encryption (TLS)
supports: All serverless caches have in-transit encryption enabled; node-based clusters can turn it on or off
Caches with a public endpoint require TLS 1.3

sources.title: Supported and restricted Valkey, Memcached, and Redis OSS commands
supports: EVAL and EVALSHA are listed among the commands supported by serverless caches

sources.title: Scaling ElastiCache Serverless clusters
supports: A maximum can be set on cache data storage and on ECPUs per second to control cost
At the storage maximum ElastiCache evicts keys that have a TTL, and writes fail with an out-of-memory error when nothing can be evicted; above the ECPU maximum requests are throttled
A minimum usage limit is billed even when actual usage is lower
sources.note: Neither this page nor the API reference pages for DataStorage and ECPUPerSecond state the smallest accepted maximum. The stack's ECPU maximum of 1,000 is the value the page uses in its CLI example for a minimum.

sources.title: Engine versions and upgrading in ElastiCache
supports: All features available with Redis OSS 7.2 are available in Valkey 7.2 and above
Some existing ElastiCache for Redis OSS engines can be upgraded to a Valkey engine
ElastiCache versions 9.0 and 9.1 for Valkey exist

sources.title: Amazon ElastiCache pricing
supports: Serverless is billed for data stored (GB-hours, from an hourly average) and for ECPUs; a read or write uses 1 ECPU per KB transferred, and commands needing more vCPU time use proportionally more
Minimum metered data storage is 100 MB per cache for ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey and 1 GB for Memcached and Redis OSS
Billing starts when a serverless cache becomes available and continues until it is deleted
Accounts created before 2025-07-15 get 750 hours of cache.t3.micro for 12 months, which excludes ElastiCache Serverless; newer accounts get credits instead
Serverless with a public endpoint: no data transfer charge on the cache side, and USD 0.01 per GB in or out of the application within the same Region
Valkey is priced 33% lower than the other engines on Serverless and 20% lower on nodes
sources.note: The price tables on the page are rendered by script and were not read; unit prices come from the Price List.

sources.title: AWS Price List bulk API: ElastiCache, ap-northeast-1
supports: Unit prices in data/pricing/unit-prices.json with offerCode AmazonElastiCache
Serverless Valkey in Tokyo: USD 0.101 per GB-hour stored and USD 0.0027 per million ECPUs
A cache.t4g.micro node running Valkey in Tokyo: USD 0.02 per node-hour

sources.title: AWS::ElastiCache::ServerlessCache
supports: Properties include CacheUsageLimits, ConnectionType (vpc | public, default vpc, replacement on change), Engine (valkey | redis | memcached), MajorEngineVersion (an integer such as 9), ServerlessCacheName (required, at most 40 characters), UserGroupId, SubnetIds, SecurityGroupIds, FinalSnapshotName, and SnapshotRetentionLimit
Fn::GetAtt returns ARN, Endpoint.Address, and Endpoint.Port
CacheUsageLimits holds DataStorage (Maximum, Minimum, Unit = GB) and ECPUPerSecond (Maximum, Minimum)
sources.note: aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0 exposes the same properties on CfnServerlessCache, including connectionType.

sources.title: cdkd v0.296.28: src/provisioning/register-providers.ts
supports: Dedicated providers are registered for AWS::DynamoDB::Table, AWS::Logs::LogGroup, AWS::Lambda::Function, AWS::Lambda::Permission, AWS::IAM::Role, AWS::IAM::Policy, and the AWS::ApiGatewayV2 types the chapter 14 stack uses
For ElastiCache only AWS::ElastiCache::SubnetGroup and AWS::ElastiCache::CacheCluster have a dedicated provider; AWS::ElastiCache::ServerlessCache has none and is handled through Cloud Control API
sources.note: src/provisioning/stateful-types.ts at the same tag lists AWS::ElastiCache::ServerlessCache as a stateful type. Both were also confirmed in the bundled dist of the npm tarball.

sources.title: valkey-io/valkey README
supports: Valkey was forked from the open source Redis project right before the transition to its new source-available licenses
Valkey is a data structure server that primarily serves key/value workloads

sources.title: Valkey: Scripting with Lua
supports: Valkey guarantees a script's atomic execution; all server activities are blocked while it runs
Every key a script accesses must be passed explicitly as a key argument, in standalone and clustered deployments alike

sources.title: Valkey command: SET
supports: PXAT sets the Unix time in milliseconds at which the key expires; NX sets the key only if it does not exist
SET key value NX with an expiry is described as a simple way to implement a lock

sources.title: Valkey command: EXPIRE
supports: The expire error is from 0 to 1 milliseconds
Expired keys are reclaimed on access and by a background cycle; a key found to be timed out on access is deleted at that moment

sources.title: Valkey command: INCR
supports: INCR is an atomic increment; the page describes the counter and rate limiter patterns built on it

sources.title: valkey/valkey container image tags (Docker Hub)
supports: Tag 9.0.6-alpine exists (last updated 2026-09-21)
sources.note: Read through the Docker Hub tags API. The image was not pulled or run; the contract tests ran against valkey-server 9.1.2 from nixpkgs instead.

sources.title: iovalkey 0.4.0 (npm registry metadata and tarball)
supports: 0.4.0 was the latest version, published 2026-07-27, MIT, with no native or platform-specific dependencies
Exports Redis (also as Valkey) and Cluster; RedisOptions.username and password are plain strings
On connect, AUTH is sent before any other command when a password is set (built/redis/event_handler.js)
The README recommends dnsLookup: (address, callback) => callback(null, address) with redisOptions.tls for ElastiCache clusters with TLS
valkey:// and valkeys:// URLs are accepted

sources.title: @valkey/valkey-glide 2.5.3 (npm registry metadata)
supports: 2.5.3 was the latest version, published 2026-09-24, Apache-2.0
Its native code ships as optional dependencies per platform: darwin-x64, darwin-arm64, linux-x64-gnu, linux-x64-musl, linux-arm64-gnu, linux-arm64-musl
sources.note: Only the registry metadata was read. The package was not installed, and its IAM configuration for Node.js was not checked against its types.

sources.title: Understanding the Lambda execution environment lifecycle
supports: After an invocation Lambda freezes the execution environment and keeps it for some time in anticipation of another invocation
Lambda terminates execution environments every few hours for runtime updates and maintenance, even for functions invoked continuously
Objects declared outside the handler stay initialized when the environment is reused

sources.title: Understanding Lambda function scaling
supports: Concurrency is the number of in-flight requests a function handles at the same time; for each concurrent request Lambda provisions a separate instance of the execution environment

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers KV: Pricing
supports: Workers KV is included in the Free and Paid Workers plans
Free: 100,000 reads, 1,000 writes, 1,000 deletes, 1,000 list requests per day, and 1 GB stored
Paid: 10 million reads and 1 million writes a month included, then USD 0.50 per million reads and USD 5.00 per million writes; 1 GB stored included, then USD 0.50 per GB-month
sources.note: The pages 'How KV works' (source cloudflare-kv-how-it-works) and 'Limits' (cloudflare-kv-limits) were re-read the same day; the statements recorded there still stand, and How KV works also says KV is not ideal where atomic operations are needed and points to Durable Objects.

sources.title: Cloudflare: What are Durable Objects?
supports: Each Durable Object has a globally unique name and is single-threaded
Each has its own durable, transactional, strongly consistent storage, accessible only within that object
In-memory state is reset when the object hibernates after being idle

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Rate Limiting binding
supports: A rate limit is defined by a limit and a period of 10 or 60 seconds
Limits are local to the Cloudflare location the Worker runs in
The API is described as permissive, eventually consistent, and not intended as an accurate accounting system

definition.ja: time to live。データに付ける有効期限。期限が来たデータをいつ実際に消すかは store によって違い、DynamoDB では数日後になることがある。
definition.en: Time to live: an expiry attached to a piece of data. When expired data is actually removed depends on the store; in DynamoDB it can be days later.

definition.ja: ある利用者が一定時間に呼べる回数の上限。数える場所が全員に共有されていて、数えて比べる操作が 1 ステップでないと守れない。
definition.en: A cap on how many calls one caller may make in a period. It holds only if the counter is shared by everyone and counting and comparing are a single step.

definition.ja: 時間を決まった長さの区間に切り、区間ごとに回数を数える rate limit の方式。区間の境目をまたぐと、短い時間に上限の 2 倍まで通る。
definition.en: A rate limit that cuts time into equal periods and counts per period. Around a boundary it lets up to twice the limit through in a short time.

definition.ja: 直前の区間の回数を、いまの時刻から見てまだ窓に入っている割合だけ数に入れる rate limit の方式。境目での 2 倍を防ぐ。
definition.en: A rate limit that also counts the previous period, in proportion to how much of it the window still covers. It prevents the doubling at a boundary.

definition.ja: 読んでから書くのではなく、「1 足す」を store の中の 1 ステップとして行う更新。同時に来た加算が失われない。
definition.en: An update that adds one as a single step inside the store instead of reading and then writing, so concurrent increments are not lost.

definition.ja: メモリ上の key-value サーバー。Redis がライセンスを変える直前のオープンソース版から分かれたプロジェクトで、ElastiCache のエンジンの 1 つ。
definition.en: An in-memory key-value server, forked from open source Redis right before its license changed, and one of the engines ElastiCache runs.

definition.ja: ElastiCache Processing Unit。ElastiCache Serverless のリクエストの課金単位。単純な読み書きは、転送した 1 KB あたり 1 ECPU。
definition.en: ElastiCache Processing Unit: the billing unit for requests to ElastiCache Serverless. A simple read or write uses 1 ECPU per KB transferred.

definition.ja: まず cache を読み、無ければ元データを読んで cache に入れる読み方。正しいのは常に元データで、cache はその写し。
definition.en: Reading the cache first and, on a miss, reading the source of truth and storing a copy. The source is always right; the cache is a copy.

definition.ja: 元データが変わったあとに、古い写しを読むこと。cache を使うかぎり起きるので、どれだけ古くてよいかを先に決める。
definition.en: Reading an old copy after the source changed. It happens whenever there is a cache, so decide beforehand how old is acceptable.

definition.ja: cache が切れた瞬間に、多数のリクエストが同時に miss して、全員が元データへ取りに行くこと。
definition.en: Many requests missing at the moment an entry expires, and all of them going to the source of truth at once.

definition.ja: 同じ key の読み込みが進行中なら、新しく始めずにその結果を待つこと。効くのは 1 つのプロセスの中だけ。
definition.en: Waiting for a load of the same key that is already in progress instead of starting another. It works within one process only.

title.ja: KV と cache: DynamoDB 版で月 100 万リクエスト
title.en: KV and cache: one million requests a month on DynamoDB

ja: `GET /items` を月 100 万回。すべて rate limit を通る（拒否された分も書き込み 1 単位を消費する）
rate limit: リクエストごとに UpdateItem 1 回（1 KB 未満、書き込み 1 単位）。固定窓
cache の読み取り: リクエストごとに結果整合の GetItem 1 回（4 KB 未満、読み取り 0.5 単位）
cache の詰め直し: TTL 30 秒が切れるたびに必ず 1 回起きると仮定して月 87,600 回。1 回あたり lock の取得・値の書き込み・lock の解放で書き込み 3 単位、取り直しの読み取り 0.5 単位
Lambda は arm64、256 MB、平均 30 ミリ秒と仮定。ログは 1 リクエスト 0.5 KB
table の保存量は 1 MB。インターネットへのデータ転送は未算入
en: One million `GET /items` a month, all within the rate limit (a refused request consumes one write unit too)
Rate limit: one UpdateItem per request (under 1 KB, one write unit), fixed window
Cache read: one eventually consistent GetItem per request (under 4 KB, half a read unit)

Cache refill: assumed to happen every time the 30-second TTL runs out, 87,600 times a month; each takes three write units (take the lock, write the value, release the lock) and half a read unit for the re-check
Lambda on arm64 with 256 MB and an assumed average of 30 ms; 0.5 KB of logs per request
1 MB stored in the table. Data transfer out to the internet is not included

items.basis: about 7 days of logs kept, in GB-month

保存量は 100 MB 未満。最小課金 100 MB（0.1 GB として計算）を 730 時間
1 リクエストあたり 10 ECPU と多めに仮定。script（EVAL）が実際に何 ECPU を消費するかは計測していない
Lambda は arm64、256 MB、平均 30 ミリ秒と仮定。ログは 1 リクエスト 0.5 KB
public endpoint へのデータ転送（アプリ側で 1 GB あたり USD 0.01）と、インターネットへのデータ転送は未算入
DynamoDB の table は stack に残るが、この構成では読み書きしない
en: One million `GET /items` a month
Less than 100 MB stored: the 100 MB minimum (computed as 0.1 GB) for 730 hours
10 ECPUs per request assumed, on the generous side; how many ECPUs a script (EVAL) really uses was not measured
Lambda on arm64 with 256 MB and an assumed average of 30 ms; 0.5 KB of logs per request
Data transfer to the public endpoint (USD 0.01 per GB on the application side) and out to the internet is not included
The DynamoDB table stays in the stack but is not read or written in this setup

items.basis: 0.1 GB minimum x 730 hours, in GB-hours
about 7 days of logs kept, in GB-month

summary.en: The chapter 14 stack has never been deployed. Unconfirmed: that the conditional `ADD` loses no concurrent increment on the real service, how long TTL really takes to delete an item, how the memory variant behaves once Lambda runs several execution environments, and creation and deletion through cdkd 0.296.28.

resume.ja: `vp run kv:infra:deploy` のあと `vp run kv:smoke` を実行し、6 回目が 429 になることを確かめる。`vp run kv:infra:drift` を実行し、最後に `vp run kv:infra:destroy`。
resume.en: Run `vp run kv:infra:deploy`, then `vp run kv:smoke` and check that the sixth request is refused with 429. Run `vp run kv:infra:drift`, and finally `vp run kv:infra:destroy`.

summary.ja: ElastiCache Serverless（public endpoint）には一度もつないでいない。未確認: CloudFormation と Cloud Control API が `ConnectionType: public` と `UserGroupId: default.iam-user-group` を受け付けること、`CacheUsageLimits` の ECPU の上限 1,000 が有効な値であること、自作の SigV4 token を ElastiCache が受け付けること、iovalkey の `Cluster` が public endpoint で cluster の構成を読めること、TLS 1.3 での接続、script（EVAL）の ECPU 消費、cache の作成と削除にかかる時間。
summary.en: Nothing has ever connected to an ElastiCache Serverless cache with a public endpoint. Unconfirmed: that CloudFormation and Cloud Control API accept `ConnectionType: public` with `UserGroupId: default.iam-user-group`; that 1,000 is a valid ECPU maximum in `CacheUsageLimits`; that ElastiCache accepts the hand-signed SigV4 token; that iovalkey's `Cluster` can read the topology through a public endpoint; the TLS 1.3 connection; how many ECPUs a script (EVAL) uses; and how long the cache takes to create and delete.

resume.ja: 料金がかかることを承知のうえで `vp run kv:infra:deploy -c store=valkey` を実行する。`vp run kv:smoke` で store が `elasticache` と表示され、6 回目が 429 になることを確かめる。失敗したら `vp run kv:logs` で `valkey connection error`、`cache store failed`、`rate limiter failed` を探し、公式の「Connect to a cache with a public endpoint」の Troubleshooting と照らす。終わったらすぐ `vp run kv:infra:destroy -c store=valkey`。
resume.en: Knowing that it is billed, run `vp run kv:infra:deploy -c store=valkey`. Check with `vp run kv:smoke` that the store is reported as `elasticache` and the sixth request is refused. On failure, search `vp run kv:logs` for `valkey connection error`, `cache store failed`, and `rate limiter failed`, and compare with the Troubleshooting table of 'Connect to a cache with a public endpoint'. Run `vp run kv:infra:destroy -c store=valkey` as soon as you are done.
